entries.proposition: The primary statement behind the citation 'ethosuximide was ineffective against seizures in an Scn1a zebrafish model' in the Harman 2023 paper: of nine antiseizure drugs bath-applied at one concentration to scn1Lab mutant larvae (seven fish per drug), valproate, diazepam, potassium bromide and stiripentol reduced epileptiform activity; carbamazepine, ethosuximide and vigabatrin made it more frequent in some fish (ethosuximide in 4 of 7). It is a negative with a tendency to aggravation in individual fish, not a significant aggravation.
entries.snippet: As expected, most AEDs had no effect and epileptiform activity became more frequent following exposure to carbamazepine (in 2 of 7 fish), ethosuximide (4 of 7 fish) or vigabatrin (6 of 7 fish).
entries.anchor: Results, Pharmacological evaluation of scn1Lab mutant zebrafish

entries.proposition: Design limits of the pharmacology: one bath concentration per drug, seven fish per drug, a recording before and after application in the same fish, no concurrent vehicle-exposed fish described for the electrophysiology, no wild-type comparison (wild-type larvae do not have the discharges), and the mutants are scored for epileptiform events recorded in agar-embedded larvae.
entries.snippet: All drugs were bath applied at a concentration of 1 mM; seven fish were tested for each drug.
entries.anchor: Results, Pharmacological evaluation of scn1Lab mutant zebrafish

entries.proposition: The authors conclude the pharmacological profile of the mutants resembles that of Dravet patients, whose seizures respond poorly to most drugs; the ketogenic diet reduced behaviour toward control levels in 7 of 10 mutants. The comparison to patients is by pattern, not by a clinical dataset.
entries.snippet: These results demonstrate that the pharmacological profile for scn1Lab mutants resembles that seen in children with DS.
entries.anchor: Results, Pharmacological evaluation of scn1Lab mutant zebrafish

entries.proposition: Figure 5 read as an image: panel A heat map of seven fish per drug: the ethosuximide row has fish 1 and 6 strongly excited (100+ and about 60 to 79 percent), fish 2 and 5 mildly excited, fish 3 unchanged, fish 7 mildly inhibited; the valproate, stiripentol, diazepam and potassium bromide rows are dark blue (inhibition) in most fish; panel B ethosuximide bar about +30 percent change in burst frequency with a large error bar and no star while valproate, stiripentol, diazepam, bromide carry stars; panel D fractional time seizing: ethosuximide bars equal before and after.
